Naomi / team,

I reviewed Umbratech's redline and attached a counsel note with suggested positions. High-level recommendations:

1) Subprocessors: Accept customer's request for prior notice and a standard 30-day review window for material new subprocessors. Do not accept unlimited veto rights; propose an Escalation + Mitigation clause instead (see p.3 of attached).

2) Cross-border transfers: We can sign the Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as the default. For US transfers where customer requires an "EU-US Addendum," we can accept that only if the customer acknowledges our operational constraints (e.g., multi-region model hosting). If Umbratech requires all processing to remain in EU, propose model-hosting-specific SLA and routing constraints rather than changing transfer clauses broadly.

3) Retention / Logs: Recommend counterproposal to 180 days for audit logs (we can provide 180 days as a standard offering). If customer insists on 90 days, confirm the specific logs they mean (full token-level logs vs. anonymized operational logs).

4) Evidence for subprocessors: we can provide attestations and SOC2 summary pages, but vendor contracts (NDA/POC docs) will not be shareable; produce a redacted evidence bundle instead.

Execution path: propose we produce a revised DPA (Proposed_DPA_Redline_v2.docx), capture internal approvals, then send a DocuSign envelope to Umbratech legal with the attachment.

I've attached a short PDF with inline comments for Clara's team.

-marissa
